My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

The world is a dangerous place

issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together' directly conflicts with 'I can talk about what happened very easily.' For a severe mugging-related PTSD profile, markedly fragmented recall and very easy verbal access to the trauma narrative are hard to reconcile as describing the same current memory presentation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The Memory node is internally incoherent for a severe mugging/robbery PTSD presentation: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' suggests low avoidance and relatively integrated, verbally accessible trauma memory, whereas simultaneously endorsing very vivid detailed recall and body-based painful reliving implies a highly sensory, distressing, poorly integrated trauma memory. This combination is possible in milder cases, but here it is hard to reconcile clinically within the same Memory profile. The Negative Appraisals items are coherent for robbery trauma, but the Memory selections do not fit cleanly with that node pattern or with the strong Negative Appraisals ↔ Memory linkage in the formulation.

issues.item: Constant Vigilance: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next
issues.explanation: This item is more characteristic of ongoing threat/safety behavior than of a pure negative appraisal. In this profile, Threat is not endorsed and all Threat-related edges are inactive, while the active formulation is specifically centered on a Memory ↔ Negative Appraisals loop. The mistrust items fit robbery-related appraisals, but 'Constant Vigilance' introduces a prominent current-threat theme that is not supported elsewhere in the profile.

vignette: Sandeep, a 32-year-old South Asian man married to his high school sweetheart, works as a housekeeper in a large suburban home. He has always prided himself on being meticulous and reliable, but since the mugging that occurred six months ago, he finds it increasingly difficult to perform his duties without feeling constantly on edge. The traumatic event unfolded one evening after work when Sandeep was walking back from the bus stop to the house where he lived with his wife. It was dark, and as he passed by a dimly lit alleyway, a shadowy figure emerged suddenly, brandishing a knife. The intruder demanded all of Sandeep's money, and when Sandeep hesitated, the attacker slashed him across the arm. The pain was searing, and it left an indelible mark on his psyche as much as it did on his body. Since then, every time he tries to recall that night, the memory is so vivid and painful that he feels the slash again on his arm. He can almost smell the metal of the knife, see the glint in the attacker's eye under the streetlight, hear the harsh demands, and feel the raw fear gripping him at the moment of confrontation. Despite this clarity, Sandeep struggles to put these sensations into words. The memory is so intense that it leaves him feeling paralyzed with a sense of helplessness. Sandeep's mistrust has only deepened since the mugging. He now believes that people are not what they seem and cannot be trusted. This belief extends beyond strangers; even those he once considered friends now appear suspicious to him. The world, in his view, is an unsafe place where danger lurks around every corner. His fear is palpable as he walks home from work or passes by the same alleyway, where he feels the same overwhelming dread that haunted him on that fateful night. This pervasive distrust has begun to affect his relationship with his wife and his job. At home, Sandeep finds himself increasingly distant, wary of letting anyone in too closely for fear they might betray him. He no longer opens up about his day or shares his deepest fears with her, creating a rift that strains their once-strong bond. At work, he avoids socializing with other staff members and often works late to ensure the house is secure before leaving. This behavior has led to misunderstandings and conflicts with his employer, who perceives him as aloof and uncooperative. Sandeep's performance reviews have started to reflect this tension, putting his job security at risk. What frightens Sandeep most is not just the recurring flashbacks but the realization that he might never feel safe again. He has come to believe that trusting others is a sign of weakness, a vulnerability that could lead to another attack. Yet, he also understands that avoiding everyone and everything that reminds him of that night will only isolate him further. Sandeep finally decided to seek help after his wife expressed her concern about their growing distance and the impact it was having on both of them. He hopes that with therapy, he can find a way to regain some sense of normalcy in his life without feeling like every shadow could be a threat. He is cautiously optimistic but remains deeply afraid that the world will never feel safe again.
